description: What does "hello world".split() return?
explanation: split() with no argument breaks a string on whitespace and returns a list of the pieces.

description: What does "-".join(["a", "b", "c"]) return?
explanation: join() glues the items of a list together, placing the string it was called on between each pair.
hint: The separator is the string join() is called on.

description: What does "  spaces  ".strip() return?
explanation: strip() removes whitespace from both ends of a string but leaves the inside untouched.

description: What does "banana".replace("a", "o") return?
explanation: replace() swaps every occurrence by default, so all three a characters become o.

description: What does "hello".find("l") return?
explanation: find() returns the index of the first match. The first l in hello sits at index 2.

description: What does an f-string such as f"Age: {age}" do?
explanation: An f-string inserts the current value of each expression written in braces directly into the text.
choice1: Inserts the value of age into the text
choice2: Creates a template that must be filled in later

description: What does "python"[1:4] return?
explanation: A slice starts at the first index and stops just before the second, so characters 1, 2 and 3 are taken: "yth".
hint: A slice includes the start and excludes the end.

description: What does [10, 20, 30, 40][:2] return?
explanation: Leaving the start blank means "from the beginning", so this takes the first two items.

description: What does [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][::2] return?
explanation: The third slice value is the step. A step of 2 takes every second item, starting from the first.

description: What does "abcdef"[::-1] return?
explanation: A step of -1 walks the string backwards, which reverses it.

description: What does [1, 2] + [3, 4] evaluate to?
explanation: Adding two lists concatenates them into one longer list rather than adding the numbers.

description: What is the difference between append() and extend() on a list?
explanation: append() adds its argument as one single item, while extend() adds each item of an iterable separately.
choice0: append() adds one item, extend() adds each item of an iterable
choice1: append() adds each item, extend() adds one item

description: What does [5, 3, 1].sort() return?
explanation: sort() rearranges the list in place and returns None. Use sorted() when you want a new list back.
hint: One of sort() and sorted() returns a value; the other changes the list itself.

description: Which method removes and returns the last item of a list?
explanation: pop() with no argument removes the final item and hands it back to you.

description: What does [1, 2, 3].index(3) return?
explanation: index() returns the position of the first matching item. The value 3 sits at index 2.

description: What does the count() method of a list do?
explanation: count() reports how many times a given value appears in the list.
choice0: Returns how many times a value appears
choice1: Returns the length of the list
choice3: Adds one to every number in the list

description: What does the keys() method of a dictionary give you?
explanation: keys() gives a view of every key in the dictionary, without their values.

description: How do you add a new entry "city": "Oslo" to a dictionary named d?
explanation: Assigning to a key that does not exist yet creates it.

description: What does d.get("missing") return when the key is not in the dictionary?
explanation: get() returns None instead of raising an error, which makes it safer than square-bracket access.

description: What happens if you write d["missing"] for a key that is not in the dictionary?
explanation: Square-bracket access on an absent key raises a KeyError.
choice1: It creates the key with value None

description: What does the items() method of a dictionary return?
explanation: items() yields each entry as a key and value pair, which is why it is convenient in for loops.

description: Can a Python dictionary contain the same key twice?
explanation: Keys are unique. Assigning to an existing key replaces the old value rather than adding a second entry.
choice0: Yes, values are then stored in a list
choice1: No, assigning again replaces the value
choice2: Yes, but only for string keys
choice3: Yes, and both are kept in order

description: What numbers does range(2, 6) produce?
explanation: range starts at the first number and stops before the second, giving 2, 3, 4 and 5.

description: What numbers does range(0, 10, 3) produce?
explanation: The third argument is the step, so the sequence advances by 3 each time: 0, 3, 6, 9.

description: What does enumerate() give you when looping over a list?
explanation: enumerate() yields the index alongside the item, so you do not need a separate counter.
choice1: The index and the item together

description: What does zip([1, 2], ["a", "b"]) let you do?
explanation: zip() pairs items from several sequences position by position, so you can walk them together.
choice0: Compress the lists to save memory
choice1: Join the lists end to end
choice3: Loop over both lists in step

description: When does the else block of a for loop run?
explanation: A for/else block runs its else only when the loop finished normally without hitting a break.
choice0: When the loop finished without break
choice3: When the loop raised an error

description: What does def greet(name="friend") define?
explanation: A default value makes the parameter optional. Calling greet() with no argument uses "friend".
choice0: A function that must always be given a name
choice1: A function that returns the text friend
choice2: A function whose name argument is optional
choice3: A function that only accepts the value friend

description: What does a function return if it has no return statement?
explanation: A function without a return statement hands back None.

description: What is a docstring?
explanation: A docstring is a string literal placed as the first statement in a function, class or module to describe it.
choice0: A string at the start of a function describing what it does
choice2: A special type of variable name
choice3: A file listing all functions in a project

description: In the call area(width=3, height=4), what are width and height called?
explanation: Naming the parameters at the call site makes them keyword arguments, which can be given in any order.

description: Which of these values is treated as False in a condition?
explanation: Empty containers, empty strings, 0 and None are all falsy. A string containing "0" is not empty, so it is truthy.

description: What does bool("") evaluate to?
explanation: An empty string is falsy, so bool("") is False. Any non-empty string is True.

description: What does 5 > 3 and 2 > 4 evaluate to?
explanation: The first comparison is True but the second is False, and and needs both sides to be True.

description: What does float("3.5") return?
explanation: float() parses a string that looks like a number and returns it as a floating-point value.

description: What does int(9.8) return?
explanation: Converting a float to an int truncates towards zero, dropping the decimal part rather than rounding.

description: What does list("abc") return?
explanation: list() breaks any iterable into its items, and a string iterates character by character.

description: What kind of error is raised by int("hello")?
explanation: The text is not a valid number, so Python raises a ValueError: the type is right but the value is not.

description: What kind of error is raised by using a variable that was never assigned?
explanation: Python raises a NameError when a name cannot be found anywhere in scope.

description: What kind of error is raised by [1, 2, 3][5]?
explanation: Asking for a position beyond the end of a list raises an IndexError.

description: What is the purpose of a try block?
explanation: A try block lets you attempt code that might fail and handle the failure in an except block instead of crashing.
choice0: To repeat code until it works
choice1: To test whether code is fast enough
choice2: To run code that might raise an error and handle it
choice3: To ignore all errors in a program

description: What does "1" + 1 raise in Python?
explanation: Python will not silently mix a string with a number, so it raises a TypeError.

description: What does import math do?
explanation: It loads the math module so its contents can be used through the math name, such as math.sqrt.
choice0: Copies every math function into your file directly
choice1: Makes the math module available as math
choice2: Runs all the code in your file through math
choice3: Installs the math package from the internet

description: What does from math import sqrt do?
explanation: It brings only sqrt into the current namespace, so you call it as sqrt() with no math prefix.
choice1: Imports math but renames it sqrt
choice2: Creates a new module called sqrt
choice3: Imports only sqrt, usable without the math prefix

description: What makes a set different from a list?
explanation: A set holds only unique items and does not preserve a meaningful order.
choice0: A set holds only unique items and is unordered
choice1: A set can only hold numbers
choice2: A set cannot be changed once created

description: What does set([1, 2, 2, 3]) return?
explanation: Building a set removes duplicates, leaving {1, 2, 3}.

description: What is the difference between == and is?
explanation: == asks whether two values are equal, while is asks whether they are the very same object in memory.
choice1: == compares values, is compares object identity

description: What does the += operator do in count += 1?
explanation: It is shorthand for count = count + 1.
choice0: Adds 1 to count and stores the result back in count
choice2: Creates a new variable named count1
choice3: Adds 1 only if count is positive

description: Why is print("a", "b") different from print("a" + "b")?
explanation: print() joins several arguments with a space by default, whereas + concatenates with nothing between.
choice2: The first prints a b with a space, the second prints ab
choice3: The second prints a b with a space

description: Where can a variable created inside a function be used?
explanation: A variable assigned inside a function is local to that call and disappears when the function returns.
choice2: Only in functions in the same file
